title: Useful MCP tools to help with game dev.
author: ResenhaDoBar
selftext: Wanted to get some recommendations of MCP tools you guys have implemented into your workflows that helped save some time. Interested in anything that could save time, 2d to 3d games, just want to get to know some cool tools I can test out to help me save time in future projects.

comments.author: jankjig
comments.body: There are plentiful sets of MCP tools for both unity and unreal on github. I use codex and unreal and had it build off of the base tools I found and now codex has a crazy amount of control with unreal. The same can be done with most game engines.

replies.author: ResenhaDoBar
replies.body: Do you know of an aggregated list with them? I'm currently working with Godot, Phaser and ThreeJS games

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
Not an MCP exactly but I have an LLM wiki built up from games design, development and project management books and resources.

It helps me link together the different stands that usually belong to multiple individuals and raises lots of questions about the best way to work with AI in an organized way. I can also throw in random blogs or posts that I think have an interesting take and it all gets absorbed.

comments.author: AgenticGameDev
comments.body: I use Unity mcp and coplay. But mostly I use my own Testrunner MooseRunner. But that is a CLI, so not a MCP. But same concept. I believe in AI TDD. It works great for me. I sadly have very limited time for reasons. But I’m blown away by what’s possible. I just added vision video + images and it’s actually can catch problems I hade to bounce my self before. So sure there is built in test tool in Unity so you don’t need what I build to get started. But I highly recommend find the feedbackloop so ai can iterate on its own.

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
Gamelabs Studio MCP:

Just using a normal AI model like Nano Banana wont work for creating assets such as spritesheets, because AI models like nano banana cant output transparency, and image models alone have no understanding of animation.

That gap is why I built GameLab Studio [https://gamelabstudio.co](https://gamelabstudio.co) . It’s designed for game assets and it’ll generate consistent pixel-art sprites, animations and full transparent bg spritesheets for anything.

https://i.redd.it/hcchfl1vbtxg1.gif

Gamelabs Studio MCP plugs right into your agent like Cursor, to enable rapid iteration right in your code editor

[https://gamelabstudio.co/blog/mcp-setup-guide](https://gamelabstudio.co/blog/mcp-setup-guide)

We also have a seamless tileable edge-aware texture generation model

comments.author: SquirrelTomahawk
comments.body:
Low key secret man, chatgpt image 2, generate your shit like textures and sprites from there. I found a work flow between that, Godot MCP pro, godot mcp docs that flows amazing between claude code.

The models and textures it generated me makes Pixel Lab look like a scrap book. And it only cost like a dollar to generate a full sprite sheet with all animations for my character.
